prose.text:
A particle is a small part of matter or light.**
Electric charge** is a property of a particle that affects electrical pushes and pulls.
Understanding charge means connecting this property with the interactions, or effects on one another, that particles can have.
prose.source_text: 你们曾多次碰到“电”、“电荷”、“电流”这些词，并习以为常. 但是，请回答“电荷是什么？”这个问题，你们会相信，这并不那么简单.

prose.text:
An **atom** is a tiny unit of a chemical element, a kind of matter such as hydrogen.
Its **nucleus** is the small central region that contains most of the atom's mass.
An **electron** is a much lighter particle found around the nucleus.

Figure 103 shows an old, simplified picture of an atom.
The circular lines are not measured paths of electrons moving around the nucleus, and the picture is not drawn to the real size scale.

**Quantum physics** describes matter and light at tiny scales.
A **probability distribution** tells us how likely a particle is to be found in different places.
Quantum rules describe electron motion using these distributions, not fixed circular tracks.

Charge is a property of a particle, not an independent object with smaller parts inside it.
Drawing an atom's structure does not give charge a structure of its own.
prose.source_text: 例如，可以说明原子是什么. 为此，说明它的结构是怎样的，绘出原子结构图(图103)：质量大的原子核处于中心，而轻的电子绕它运动，就足够了. 但是，电荷是比原子更基本、更深一层的东西. 这是一个不能再划分为更简单的基本概念. 近代的科学也丝毫不知道电荷的“结构”.

prose.text: Figure 103
prose.label: 图 103

prose.text:
Saying that a body or particle **has electric charge** describes how it takes part in electric and magnetic effects.
Charge is not another fluid stuck onto a particle or able to exist separately from matter.
prose.source_text: 我们首先要说明的不是电荷是什么，而是如何理解某**物体或粒子具有电荷.** 理解后者是比较简单的.

prose.text:
Matter has different levels of structure.
An **elementary particle** is a particle in which no internal structure has yet been observed, and the electron is an example.
A **composite particle**, by contrast, has smaller constituents.

Not every elementary particle has nonzero rest mass, the mass belonging to the particle itself rather than its motion.
A **photon**, a packet of light energy, has zero rest mass but still carries energy.

Gravity is the attraction described by Newton's law of gravitation.
A **point model** treats an object's size as negligible compared with the distance between objects.
Newton's law approximates attraction between objects with mass when gravity is weak, speeds are low compared with the speed of light, and this point model is suitable.

In this model, the force varies inversely with the square of the distance.
This means that doubling the distance leaves one quarter of the original force, with the masses unchanged.
More generally, gravity involves energy and momentum, a measure of motion, so this approximate law cannot simply be applied to all particles.
prose.source_text: 你们知道，所有物体都是由最小的、不可再分为更简单的(就目前科学所知)粒子所组成的，因此，这些粒子叫做**基本粒子**. 所有的基本粒子都具有质量，从而它们彼此按照万有引力相互吸引，引力的大小与它们之间的距离平方成反比.

prose.text:
An **electromagnetic field** describes electric and magnetic conditions at each place that can affect particles.**
Electromagnetic interactions** are the effects involving these fields.
A **charged particle** has nonzero electric charge.

A photon is electrically neutral, meaning that its electric charge is zero.
It is nevertheless a quantum of the electromagnetic field, a packet of energy exchanged through that field.
Being uncharged does not make it unrelated to electromagnetic phenomena.

For stationary point charges in vacuum, space without matter, the static electric force varies inversely with the square of the distance.
With the charges unchanged, doubling their distance leaves one quarter of the original force.
Moving charges also have magnetic effects, which this static rule alone does not describe.

A **proton** is a positively charged particle in an atom's nucleus.
For an electron and a proton at the same separation, the static electric and Newtonian gravity models give an electric attraction about $10^{39}$ times as strong as their gravitational attraction.
This comparison is specific to an electron and a proton, not a ratio shared by arbitrary particles.
prose.source_text: 此外，虽然不是所有的，但绝大多数的基本粒子，还具有也是与距离平方成反比的彼此相互作用力，但是这个力比万有引力要大很多倍. **如果粒子具有这种相互作用本领，则就****说它们具有电荷，而粒子本身叫做带电粒子.** 可以有没有电荷的粒子，但不存在没有粒子的电荷. 带电粒子之间的相互作用叫做电磁相互作用. 例如，在氢原子中，电子与原子核之间的电吸引力比万有引力大$10^{39}$倍.

prose.text:
The **amount and sign of charge** help determine a charged particle's electromagnetic force, together with its position, the field there, and its motion.
For stationary point charges, both charge amounts affect the strength of their electric interaction.
The force also depends on their separation and surrounding material, so charge alone does not determine it.
prose.source_text: 跟引力质量确定了引力相互作用的强度一样，**电荷的量**确定了电磁相互作用的强度.

prose.text:
The **net force** is the combined effect of all the forces on a particle.
A charged particle can have zero net force, for example when forces cancel, so having charge does not mean always feeling a nonzero push or pull.

To understand charge, we study how charged particles produce fields and how they respond to fields.
Experiments let us measure charge and investigate these rules.
A supposed separate charged fluid cannot replace this explanation.
prose.source_text: 粒子**具有电荷**，就表示它们之间存在有一定的相互作用力. 但是，**如果我们不知道这种相互作用的规律，就丝毫不知道电荷的本质. 相互作用规律的知识应当包括**在电荷的概念中. 这些规律不是简单的，用几句话来描述它们是不可能的. **这就是为什么不能给电荷是什么一个相当**满意的简短定义的原因.

prose.text:
**Two signs of charge** are called positive and negative.
Under the conditions for Newton's gravity model, objects with positive mass attract one another.
Static electric forces can instead be attractive, pulling particles together, or repulsive, pushing them apart.

For stationary point charges in vacuum, charges with the same sign repel, while charges with opposite signs attract.
In extended bodies, charge is spread over different places and can sometimes move around.
The total charge signs alone therefore do not tell us every local force or settle all interactions between such bodies.
prose.source_text: **两种电荷** 万有引力和电力**不仅是量**值不同. 所有物体**都具有质量，因此，它们彼此相互吸引.** 带电体之间彼此可以吸引，也可以排斥. 这个在七年级物理课程中已经知道的重要事实表明：**在自然界中具有带相反符号电荷的粒子. 当电荷的符号相同时，粒子互相排斥；而当电荷的符号相反时，粒子互相吸引.**

prose.text:
By the usual naming convention, **protons have positive charge and electrons have negative charge**.
Positive and negative are signs of a property, not names for different charged fluids.
They do not imply that protons and electrons have the same mass or internal structure.

If we exchange the positive and negative labels for all charges and the corresponding electric and magnetic fields together, the physical interactions described remain unchanged.
This changes the naming convention, not the actual particles.
Replacing an electron with a different particle is not the same operation.
prose.source_text: 组成原子核的**质子**这个基本粒子的电荷，叫做**正电荷，而**电子的电荷叫做负电荷. 正电荷和负电荷之间没有任何**内部的不同.** 假如把粒子的电荷符号互换，则电磁相互作用的**特性没有**丝毫改变.

prose.text:
**Elementary charge** is a standard charge amount based on the electron's charge.
Other charged particles also exist besides electrons and protons.
The original book mentions lifetimes of a few millionths of a second, but this is not a rule for all other charged particles.

It is not true that only electrons and protons can remain stable while free.
An **antiparticle** is a partner particle with the same mass and, for a charged particle, the opposite electric charge.
The electron's antiparticle is called the **positron**.

**Decay** means that a particle transforms into other particles without a collision being needed.
A positron does not disappear through spontaneous decay in vacuum.
It can nevertheless disappear through an interaction when it meets an electron, so stability against decay differs from survival in a particular environment.

High-energy collisions can create particles.
Decay and other interactions can change which particles are present.
These processes do not release charge as a separate fluid.
prose.source_text: **基本电荷** 除了电子和质子以外，还有很多带电的**基本粒子**. 但是，**只有**电子和质子能长时间地处于自由状态. 其他带电粒子的寿命只有百万分之几秒. 它们是在高速基本粒子碰撞时诞生，存在很短的时间之后消灭，又转变为其他粒子. 你们在十年级将学习这些粒子.

prose.text:
A **neutron** is a particle with zero net electric charge and slightly more mass than a proton.
Atomic nuclei contain protons, and many also contain neutrons.

A **quark** is an elementary particle that is a constituent of composite particles.
Protons and neutrons are made of quarks, so neither is an elementary particle with no observed internal structure.
Quarks are confined within composite particles rather than being observed as freely separated particles.
prose.source_text: 中子是不带电荷的粒子. 中子的质量比质子的质量稍大一点. 中子和质子一起组成原子核.

prose.text:
Elementary particles need not be electrically charged.**
Charge quantization** means that charge amounts occur in definite steps, not like a fluid amount that can take any value we choose.
The original book names Millikan and Joffe among the scientists whose experiments investigated this step-like behavior.

For an isolated body made of ordinary atomic matter, considered as a whole, the net charge is a whole-number multiple of the elementary charge, and can be positive, negative, or zero.
This statement is limited to that kind of matter and that whole-body description.
prose.source_text: 总之，基本粒子不一定带电. 但是，如果它有电荷，则正如多数实验所指出的，电荷的数量是严格一定的(其中一个实验是七年级课本里曾描述的密立根和约飞实验).

historical_entities.reason: 保留原书电荷量子化实验史所述真实研究者，不把其身份改成虚构人物。
保留原书对电荷量子化实验史研究者的姓名写法，不补造具体实验分工或测量结果。

prose.text:
The **elementary charge**, written e, is defined to be positive and equal to the magnitude of the electron's charge.
Here **magnitude** means the amount without its positive or negative sign.
An electron has a negative elementary charge, while a proton has a positive elementary charge.

This does not make e the smallest nonzero charge of every kind of particle.
Charged particles do not all differ only in the sign of their charge.
Quantization in ordinary isolated matter does not mean that e is a fluid that can be cut into arbitrary pieces, as the quark discussion explains in note ①.
prose.source_text: 所有**带电基本粒子具有的最小电荷，叫做基本电荷.** 基本粒子的电荷只是符号不同①.

prose.text:
① Experiments now support the existence of quarks, rather than leaving them as an unconfirmed hypothesis.
Quarks and their antiparticles have charge amounts whose magnitudes are $\frac{1}{3}$ or two thirds of the elementary charge.
The positive or negative sign depends on the kind of quark or antiparticle.

**Confinement** means that quarks remain bound within composite particles, and freely isolated quarks have not been observed.
Fractional quark charges inside these particles do not mean that ordinary isolated bodies can acquire arbitrary fractions of the elementary charge.
They also do not mean that an electron's charge can be divided into any pieces we choose.
prose.label: footnote
prose.source_text: ① 不久前曾发表了一种假说，存在有带$\frac{1}{3}$基本电荷的粒子，叫做夸克. 假定质子、中子和其他重的基本粒子都是由夸克组成的. 然而，目前还不能用实验发现夸克.

data.title: 电荷和基本粒子

prose.text: 你们曾多次碰到“电”、“电荷”、“电流”这些词，并习以为常. 但是，请回答“电荷是什么？”这个问题，你们会相信，这并不那么简单.
例如，可以说明原子是什么. 为此，说明它的结构是怎样的，绘出原子结构图(图103)：质量大的原子核处于中心，而轻的电子绕它运动，就足够了. 但是，电荷是比原子更基本、更深一层的东西. 这是一个不能再划分为更简单的基本概念. 近代的科学也丝毫不知道电荷的“结构”.
我们首先要说明的不是电荷是什么，而是如何理解某**物体或粒子具有电荷.** 理解后者是比较简单的.
你们知道，所有物体都是由最小的、不可再分为更简单的(就目前科学所知)粒子所组成的，因此，这些粒子叫做**基本粒子**. 所有的基本粒子都具有质量，从而它们彼此按照万有引力相互吸引，引力的大小与它们之间的距离平方成反比.
此外，虽然不是所有的，但绝大多数的基本粒子，还具有也是与距离平方成反比的彼此相互作用力，但是这个力比万有引力要大很多倍. **如果粒子具有这种相互作用本领，则就****说它们具有电荷，而粒子本身叫做带电粒子.** 可以有没有电荷的粒子，但不存在没有粒子的电荷. 带电粒子之间的相互作用叫做电磁相互作用. 例如，在氢原子中，电子与原子核之间的电吸引力比万有引力大$10^{39}$倍.
跟引力质量确定了引力相互作用的强度一样，**电荷的量**确定了电磁相互作用的强度.
粒子**具有电荷**，就表示它们之间存在有一定的相互作用力. 但是，**如果我们不知道这种相互作用的规律，就丝毫不知道电荷的本质. 相互作用规律的知识应当包括**在电荷的概念中. 这些规律不是简单的，用几句话来描述它们是不可能的. **这就是为什么不能给电荷是什么一个相当**满意的简短定义的原因.
**两种电荷** 万有引力和电力**不仅是量**值不同. 所有物体**都具有质量，因此，它们彼此相互吸引.** 带电体之间彼此可以吸引，也可以排斥. 这个在七年级物理课程中已经知道的重要事实表明：**在自然界中具有带相反符号电荷的粒子. 当电荷的符号相同时，粒子互相排斥；而当电荷的符号相反时，粒子互相吸引.**
组成原子核的**质子**这个基本粒子的电荷，叫做**正电荷，而**电子的电荷叫做负电荷. 正电荷和负电荷之间没有任何**内部的不同.** 假如把粒子的电荷符号互换，则电磁相互作用的**特性没有**丝毫改变.
**基本电荷** 除了电子和质子以外，还有很多带电的**基本粒子**. 但是，**只有**电子和质子能长时间地处于自由状态. 其他带电粒子的寿命只有百万分之几秒. 它们是在高速基本粒子碰撞时诞生，存在很短的时间之后消灭，又转变为其他粒子. 你们在十年级将学习这些粒子.
中子是不带电荷的粒子. 中子的质量比质子的质量稍大一点. 中子和质子一起组成原子核.
总之，基本粒子不一定带电. 但是，如果它有电荷，则正如多数实验所指出的，电荷的数量是严格一定的(其中一个实验是七年级课本里曾描述的密立根和约飞实验).
所有**带电基本粒子具有的最小电荷，叫做基本电荷.** 基本粒子的电荷只是符号不同①.
① 不久前曾发表了一种假说，存在有带$\frac{1}{3}$基本电荷的粒子，叫做夸克. 假定质子、中子和其他重的基本粒子都是由夸克组成的. 然而，目前还不能用实验发现夸克.
